citation: Thompson, James. Plat of the Town of Chicago. Illinois and Michigan Canal Commissioners, completed 4 August 1830.
author: James Thompson
repository: Chicago History Museum (working copy, ICHi-34284); the original burned in the 1871 fire
locator: chicago/pre_fire_v1/maps/images/1830_thompson_plat.png (the sheet held in this repository; read for its stated figures, never traced for geometry)
note: PARAMETER SOURCE, not a warping raster — no open high-resolution archival scan located, and the surviving artifact is a Canal Commissioners' working copy dated to at least 1836. Its value is the hard dimensional module: the original Town of Chicago at roughly 0.375 sq mi, 80-ft streets, 18-ft alleys. Generate street and alley geometry analytically from those figures rather than tracing pixels. A COPY OF THE SHEET IS HELD IN THIS REPOSITORY at chicago/pre_fire_v1/maps/images/1830_thompson_plat.png — the owner pointed T-0444 at it on 2026-09-03 for the West Division's lot dimensions and block lot-counts, which are READ off it as figures; the rule above still governs geometry. `verified` flips to true in the commit that reads it. READ FOR ITS WATERCOURSES on 2026-09-04 under T-0452, at 5x on the repository copy: the sheet draws ONE watercourse and only one — two freehand banks running north out of the main stem across North Division block 6, crossing the block's alley and North Water Street and flaring at the mouth — and draws none anywhere else in the North, West or South Divisions. It is therefore NOT the source of the "three sloughs off the Main Branch" count, which is Conley/Stelzer 1933's; see docs/RESEARCH/thompson_plat_sloughs.md. The reading is of what is drawn and where, by block and lot; no course is traced from it, the rule above still governing geometry. GEOREFERENCED 2026-09-05 under T-0685, and this does NOT relax the rule above. Twenty-two street-corridor crossings on the repository copy were matched to modern OpenStreetMap intersections in EPSG:26916 - the same control method as wright_1834_gcps.json - and fitted conformally at RMS 4.9 m (data/traces/gcp/thompson_1830_gcps.json). The fit exists to MEASURE this sheet against geometry the project already stands on; no street, lot, block or building is derived from it, and geometry is still generated from the stated figures. The one thing traced through it is the river at the forks (data/traces/vectors/thompson_1830_forks_banks.json), committed BESIDE the Wright 1834 planform as evidence and not as the planform of record. What that measured: along the main stem the two north banks agree to 13 m east of local E +200 and 18 m west of it, but on the NORTH BRANCH this sheet draws the east bank 27-43 m west of the Wright line, the west bank 35-60 m west, and the channel 20 m wider, over the whole reach from the point to local N +240. That is more than the +/-20 m of georeference uncertainty the project declares, and it is structured rather than noisy - both banks displaced west together over 240 m, the fit able to account for about 3 m of it. THE OWNER RULED ON IT, 2026-09-05: WRIGHT 1834 REMAINS THE PLANFORM OF RECORD AND NOTHING MOVES. Wright is a survey OF the river, four years nearer the scene, with the river as its subject; this sheet's river is a boundary on a plat of lots, drawn freehand on a working copy dated to at least 1836. So the Thompson banks stay committed BESIDE the Wright planform as evidence and are not the planform of record, the rule at the top of this note still governs geometry, and no waterline, landing, heightfield or frontage rule is re-derived. What the ruling does NOT do is make the two sheets agree: the 27-60 m stands as measured and is the honest uncertainty at Wolf Point. See docs/RESEARCH/thompson_forks_georeference.md and ticket T-0685. READ FOR THE WEST DIVISION'S LOT FIGURES on 2026-09-13 under T-0689, paying T-0444's acceptance point 1: 22 blocks, 203 lots, every figure citing the pixel region of this file it was read on, in data/traces/thompson_west_division_lots.json and docs/RESEARCH/west_division_lot_figures.md. The sheet prints lot depth 180 ft, lot frontage 75 3/5 ft, ten lots to a standard block in two columns of five across a north-south alley, and 80 ft streets; 180 + 18 + 180 and 5 x 75 3/5 both give 378 ft from inputs that share nothing, so the block is square and the 458 ft module of docs/RESEARCH/west_division_module.md comes back from figures instead of inferences. The reading is held to this file's sha256 by tools/read_west_division_lots.py --check. NOTE THE SHEET'S OWN N.B.: the dimension figures are the Book A page 318 hand's additions, 'noted in blue figures hereon', not necessarily Thompson's of 4 August 1830. The no-tracing rule above still governs geometry and nothing was traced.
